content: Sports game results are almost always findable with 2-3 targeted searches. Use '[Team A] vs [Team B] [date] result' or '[Team A] [Team B] final score [date]'. ESPN game summaries and Wikipedia are most reliable.

For temporal prediction tasks, the resolution date is critical. When an outcome was later reversed (e.g., AFCON 2025: Senegal won on pitch Jan 18 but CAF overturned in March 2026), use the state AT the resolution date.

Prediction market resolution data is highly reliable. When Manifold Markets shows '99%+ for option X' or 'resolved Jan 14', this is strong evidence of the actual outcome. Search 'Manifold [event] resolved' to find this data.

NASA GISTEMP uses 1951-1980 baseline. NOAA uses 20th century average (1901-2000). GISTEMP anomalies are ~0.1-0.15°C LOWER than NOAA for the same month. Dec 2025 NOAA=1.05°C, GISTEMP≈0.90-0.95°C (<1.095°C threshold).
UK ONS Labour Market Overview releases monthly. Jan 2026 release covers Sep-Nov 2025 period. Sep-Nov 2025 UK unemployment was 5.1% (up from 5.0% in Jul-Sep 2025, up to 5.2% in Oct-Dec 2025).
Eurozone Dec 2024 inflation was 2.4% (Eurostat flash estimate Jan 7, 2025). Canada Dec 2024 CPI was 1.8% YoY (GST/HST holiday effect). These are historical data points for reference.

For multi-select questions ('identify ALL correct options'), missing any correct option OR including any wrong option results in penalty. Be thorough but precise. When evidence is strong for an option, include it.

Search efficiency: For straightforward factual lookups (sports scores, economic data), 2-5 searches are sufficient. Avoid excessive searching (20+ calls) when initial searches yield clear results. Stop when you have confirmed data.

Box Office Mojo holiday weekend reporting: For MLK weekend, BOM reports the 4-day figure as 'opening weekend'. Example: '28 Years Later: The Bone Temple' (Jan 2026) had 3-day=$13M but BOM reported $15M (4-day) as opening weekend. Always check if it's a holiday weekend before interpreting box office figures.

Niche personal Manifold markets (e.g., 'In which city will Tetraspace be on Jan 15?') are very hard to resolve without direct market access. When unable to find resolution, consider: (1) which options were listed as specific (suggesting they were expected), (2) the person's known patterns, (3) 'Other' as a fallback if truly uncertain. Don't waste 20+ searches on these.
